PMID:42151745.topic: Modifiable risk factor management in hip and knee osteoarthritis
PMID:42151745.setting: NHS Orthopaedic Interface Service (advanced practitioner-led), Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, South West England
PMID:42151745.standard: Best practice guidance (NHS England 2025) on identifying and acting on modifiable risk factors (weight, smoking, diabetes, psychosocial); aim to increase proportion of applicable consultations with documented action on at least one factor; no numeric target stated

cycle1.dates: January to June 2024 (retrospective audit); August to September 2025 (prospective baseline)
cycle1.result: Retrospective audit: action documented in 11% of consultations. Prospective baseline: documented action in 30% (3/10) in August and 39% (7/18) in September 2025 of applicable consultations; baseline median 34.5%

PMID:42151745.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: audit feedback at team meeting, a one-page clinician handout on thresholds and local options placed in clinic rooms, then an EPIC SmartPhrase with standardised text and signposting links

cycle2.result: Documented action in 78% (14/18) of applicable consultations (30 reviewed); overall 54% (49/90) across August 2025 to January 2026; weight advice or signposting for BMI ≥30 rose from 25% (2/8) in August to 86% (12/14) in January

PMID:42151745.other_findings: Smoking advice documented in 6 of 11 smokers, HbA1c documented in 5 of 13 patients with diabetes, and psychosocial factors documented in only 9 consultations; run chart did not meet formal shift or trend rules.

PMID:36601195.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, Poole General Hospital, University Hospitals Dorset (district general hospital)
PMID:36601195.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice guidance on operation notes (34-parameter checklist)

cycle1.result: 9.52% of notes typed (90.48% handwritten); 10 important parameters recorded in less than 10% of notes; emergency/elective and time never documented

PMID:36601195.intervention: Findings presented at surgical care group and governance meetings; typed operation note templates with editable fields for common procedures provided in each theatre, a dedicated printer near recovery, and templates designed with the IT team

cycle2.result: 66.67% of notes typed (33.33% handwritten); 3 important parameters still recorded in less than 10% of notes; documentation of 12 parameters improved across the three cycles

PMID:36601195.other_findings: Second cycle (14 to 21 February and 1 to 7 March 2021, n=96) had 57.14% typed notes and 4 parameters below 10%; emergency/elective status was never documented in any cycle and estimated blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis stayed poor. Consultants were slower to adopt typed templates than registrars.

PMID:32025448.setting: Emergency department and orthopaedic service, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin (tertiary referral centre)
PMID:32025448.standard: BOA/BGS Blue Book standard 1: all hip fracture patients admitted to an acute orthopaedic ward within 4 hours (240 minutes) of presentation

cycle1.result: Compliance 17.00%; mean time to ward 417 minutes; mean time to orthopaedic review 83 minutes

PMID:32025448.intervention: Policy change and protocol: on-call orthopaedic SHOs to review suspected hip fractures after the generic hip fracture alert, before definitive ED referral, with precise documentation of alert, referral, review and admission times

cycle2.result: Compliance 21.70%; mean time to ward 333 minutes (84-minute decrease, p=0.126); mean time to orthopaedic review 76 minutes

PMID:32025448.other_findings: Time to orthopaedic referral fell by 58 minutes (p=0.020) and time to X-ray ordering by 44 minutes (p=0.007), but 12.5% of referrals had no X-ray and 25% no bloods. Time of ward arrival was documented in only 70.5% of cases overall.

PMID:39870479.setting: Trauma and elective orthopaedic theatres, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust (City Hospital)
PMID:39870479.standard: Local surgical pause and imaging pause protocols (in the context of NatSSIPs/LocSSIPs); SMART aim of zero never events within 12 months

cycle1.result: 100% implementation of both surgical and imaging pauses, but uncertainty about when to observe imaging pauses

PMID:39870479.intervention: Clarified timing of imaging and surgical pauses, explained at weekly theatre staff meetings, posters displayed beside the WHO checklist, and pause protocols added to new staff induction

cycle2.result: 100% adherence to surgical and imaging pauses maintained; zero never events since 2017

PMID:39870479.other_findings: Second cycle (June to December 2021) also showed 100% implementation. Data were collected over 29 theatre days in total by staff not in the operating team; never events were 1 in 2013/14 and 2 in 2016/17.

PMID:38872313.topic: VTE prophylaxis after foot and ankle surgery
PMID:38872313.setting: 68 UK centres in the multicentre prospective UK Foot and Ankle Thrombo-Embolism Audit (UK-FATE)

cycle1.result: Among patients not receiving chemical thromboprophylaxis, symptomatic VTE rate was 0.30% (11 cases) with no VTE-related mortality; lower-risk group VTE rate 0.05% (1/1819) versus 0.67% (10/1490), P = .002

PMID:38872313.other_findings: VTE rate was highest in non-operatively managed Achilles tendon ruptures (3.12%); regression identified no single factor associated with VTE risk.

PMID:40922850.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
PMID:40922850.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro (district general hospital)
PMID:40922850.standard: BOAST guidance for paediatric supracondylar fractures: documented preoperative neurovascular assessment of radial, ulnar, median and anterior interosseous nerves, radial pulse and capillary refill

cycle1.result: 45.8% (11/24) compliant; capillary refill not documented in 11, radial pulse in 7, AIN in 4, and 3 had only 'NVI'

PMID:40922850.intervention: Results presented at audit and governance meetings, departmental emails, audit results included in resident doctor induction, standardised five-parameter assessment and tick-box neurovascular proformas distributed in ED and orthopaedics
PMID:40922850.other_findings: Of the 10 non-compliant cases in cycle 2, 4 had only 'NVI' documented and 3 lacked ED radial pulse documentation before back slab application.

PMID:40546492.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital, Lucknow (1,200-bed tertiary care institution)
PMID:40546492.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice guidance on operation notes

cycle1.result: 35.8% of parameters documented; emergency/elective, legibility, complications and extra procedures 0%; patient identification 96%, consultant and anaesthetist 90%

PMID:40546492.intervention: Two-month training programme (questionnaire, classes, awareness sessions) plus a mandatory new RCS-based operation note proforma replacing the progress sheet, and an RCS checklist placed in each file

cycle2.result: 90.2% of parameters documented; date/time 91%, emergency/elective 86%, operative findings 76%, complications 60%

PMID:40546492.other_findings: Complications (60%), incision shape (68%) and weight-bearing protocol (74%) remained the lowest items after the intervention.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.059.setting: Inpatient medical and surgical wards (excluding acute medical and surgical wards), Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.059.standard: Resuscitation Council UK ReSPECT guidance (17 criteria); target 100% in all criteria

cycle1.result: Best: CPR recommendation signature and demographics 99.3% (293); worst: mental capacity assessment in notes 15.2% (11/72) and reasoning for lack of capacity 48.6% (35/72); values and fears documented 22%

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.059.other_findings: Medical wards performed significantly better than surgical wards on reasoning for lack of capacity (p < 0.05); legal proxy documentation was very low on all wards. Education and a re-audit in 6–12 months were planned.
